check.q: A clinical letter in SharePoint has a retention label to keep it 10 years, and the site has a retention policy that deletes content after 3 years. What happens?
options: The label and policy cancel each other out
check.why: Retention wins over deletion and the longest retention period wins, so the letter is kept 10 years. The tempting idea that the site wide policy overrides the item misreads the principles. Nothing is kept forever unless a setting says so.

lessons.key: Retention policies set broad rules for locations, retention labels set item level rules, and in conflicts keeping beats deleting.

lessons.title: Records management
steps: What a record is

A **record** is business, legal or regulatory content that must be kept unchanged for a set time and then disposed of in a way you can prove. **Records management** in Purview builds on retention labels to do this.
Declaring records

A retention label can **declare an item a record**. Deleting it is then blocked. A record can be **locked**, so no edits are allowed, or **unlocked**, so edits are allowed with versions kept. A **regulatory record** is stricter still: nobody, not even a Global Administrator, can remove the label, and edits are blocked.
The file plan and events

A **file plan** holds the organisation's retention schedule in one place, with details such as category and department. **Event based retention** starts the clock when something happens, such as a contract ending or an employee leaving, rather than when the file was created.
Proof of disposal

At the end of the period, a **disposition review** lets chosen reviewers approve deletion, and Purview keeps proof of what was disposed of. Tui Bay's signed patient consent forms are declared records, kept for the required period, then reviewed and destroyed with evidence for the auditor.

check.q: Tui Bay needs signed consent forms that cannot be edited or deleted during their retention period. What should Sam apply?
options: A retention label that declares the item a record
check.why: Declaring an item a record through a retention label blocks deletion and, when locked, edits. Sensitivity labels and encryption control who can read content, not whether it can be deleted, and DLP and Conditional Access deal with sharing and sign in.

lessons.key: Records management uses retention labels to declare records that cannot be deleted, then proves disposal through disposition review.

lessons.title: Insider risk management
steps: Threats from inside

Not every threat comes from outside. **Insider risk** covers employees or contractors who leak data, steal intellectual property or break security rules, whether on purpose or by accident. A physio leaving to open a rival clinic might take the patient list with them.
Policies from templates

**Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management** builds policies from templates such as data theft by departing users, data leaks, security policy violations and risky AI usage. The departing users template can be triggered by a resignation date from an HR connector or by the account being deleted in Entra ID.
From alert to case

Activity that matches a policy raises an **alert**. Reviewers triage it, dismiss it or open a **case**, investigate the user's activity, then send the user a notice, resolve the case or escalate it to eDiscovery.
Privacy by design

Usernames are **pseudonymised** by default, so reviewers see a placeholder rather than a name until there is a reason to reveal it, and access is tightly limited and audited. **Adaptive Protection** gives users an insider risk level of minor, moderate or elevated and can apply stricter DLP rules automatically to riskier users. **Communication compliance**, a related tool, finds messages in Teams, email and Copilot that break policy.

check.q: A physio resigns, and in her last week she downloads hundreds of patient files. Which Purview solution is designed to flag this pattern?
check.why: The data theft by departing users template in insider risk management combines the resignation signal with unusual downloads. Compliance Manager tracks controls, records management keeps and disposes of records, and the Service Trust Portal holds Microsoft's documents.

lessons.key: Insider risk management uses templates and signals to flag risky insider activity while protecting privacy with pseudonymised names.

lessons.title: eDiscovery and audit
steps: Finding evidence

**Electronic discovery (eDiscovery)** is finding electronic information that may be used as evidence, for a legal case or an investigation. Purview eDiscovery searches mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams and Microsoft 365 groups.
The eDiscovery workflow

Work happens inside a **case**, which controls who can see it. Sam adds data sources such as the people involved, places a **hold** so their content cannot be permanently deleted, searches with keywords and conditions, and exports what is relevant for the lawyers. Premium features add a **review set** where results can be tagged, deduplicated and analysed.
Recording who did what

**Audit** answers who did what, where and when. **Audit (Standard)** is on by default for eligible subscriptions. It records thousands of event types across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and Entra ID in the **unified audit log**, keeps them for 180 days, and can be searched and exported.
Audit (Premium)

**Audit (Premium)** keeps key records for one year by default, allows custom retention policies, with up to 10 years using an add on licence, and records extra detail for investigations, such as which mail items were read. When a patient complains that a former partner read her notes, Sam uses audit to show exactly who opened the file and when.

check.q: Tui Bay's lawyer needs all email and Teams messages from two staff preserved before they can be deleted, for a dispute. What should Sam do first?
options: Export the audit log to CSV
Create an eDiscovery case and place a hold on those users' content
Apply a sensitivity label to their mailboxes
check.why: An eDiscovery hold preserves content so it cannot be permanently deleted while the case runs. The audit log records actions but does not preserve messages, a sensitivity label controls access rather than deletion, and an access review is about permissions.

lessons.key: eDiscovery finds and preserves evidence in cases with holds, and Audit records who did what, with Premium keeping more for longer.
